prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a continuous ground plane transitioning from a narrow walkway beside a fenced court and dirt planter in frame 1 to an open paved parking lot bordered by a sidewalk in frames 2–5, with a child and small bicycle ~2–3 m ahead and below on the right in frame 1, a tree trunk ~1.5–2 m centered in frame 2, a chain-link fence corner within ~1 m on the left in frame 3, and a large blue dumpster plus a second cyclist in a pink top ~8–15 m ahead in frames 2–5. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer walks forward past the child (who exits view after frame 1) and turns left around the fence corner in frame 3, then turns back right in frame 5 as the distant cyclist and dumpster (~1–3 m from each other) shift from the upper-right of frame 2 to the upper-left of frames 3–4 (~6–10 m away) and back to the upper-right at ~12–15 m in frame 5. Nothing is within arm's reach (~0.7 m) of the camera wearer except the left fence edge in frame 3, while the child's hands are within arm's reach of the orange bicycle handlebars in frame 1 and the second cyclist is atop their bicycle in frames 2 and 5; the tree canopy in frame 2 partially occludes the background parking lot, and the fence corner is cropped at the left border in frame 3. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground tree trunk and low shrubs (~1.5–2.5 m) from the receding parking lot surface behind them, though it is unreliable on the chain-link fence in frames 1 and 3 (filling the see-through mesh as a solid opaque wall), flattens the distant buildings into uniform black above the horizon, and lacks detail to show head or gaze orientation.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and mid-ground objects against an unlabelled black background: a 'person' mask for the child (~2–3 m ahead and below on the right) in frame 1, overlapping 'person', 'bicycle', and 'bus' masks (~10–12 m ahead on the upper right) in frame 2, a single 'bus' mask (~6–10 m ahead on the upper left) in frames 3–4, and overlapping 'person', 'motorcycle', and 'bus' masks (~12–15 m ahead on the upper right) in frame 5. In frames 2 and 5, the distant cyclist and their two-wheeled vehicle are directly in front of and within ~1–3 m of the large blue dumpster, placing the handlebars within the rider's arm's reach while all segmented objects remain well beyond the camera wearer's arm's reach across all frames. As the camera wearer moves forward and turns left then right across frames 1–5, the child leaves the field of view after frame 1, the distant rider is occluded or absent in frames 3–4 while the dumpster shifts from right to left, and the rider reappears moving rightward in front of the dumpster in frame 5. The map makes the small distant silhouette of the rider and vehicle in frames 2 and 5 immediately stand out against the cluttered parking lot background compared to RGB, but it is highly unreliable in class labelling and completeness—misclassifying the stationary blue dumpster as a 'bus' in frames 2–5, mislabelling the distant bicycle as a 'motorcycle' in frame 5, completely missing the child's orange bicycle in frame 1 as well as the nearby tree, fence, and ground layout, and providing no indication of which way people face without RGB context.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map detects only a single yellow body skeleton in the entire strip—the child standing ~2–3 m in front of and below the camera wearer on the right side of the walkway in frame 1—while frames 2–5 are completely black and show no scene layout or background objects. In frame 1, the child's torso and head keypoints orient toward the upper-left (facing roughly toward and slightly left of the camera wearer, looking up toward the wearer), with the right arm extended outward to the left and the left arm bent across the body within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) of the orange bicycle's handlebars between their legs. Across frames 2–5, as the camera wearer walks past the child and turns toward the parking lot where the second cyclist rides ~10–15 m away near the dumpster (facing right in frame 2 and away/right in frame 5 in RGB), no skeletons are rendered to track the camera wearer's turn or the distant rider's retreat. While the frame 1 skeleton makes the child's exact limb articulation, wide stance straddling the bicycle frame, and shoulder orientation clearer than the high-angle RGB view alone, the map is unreliable for broader spatial understanding because it misses the magenta hand keypoints on the child, fails to detect the distant cyclist in frames 2 and 5, and omits all environmental obstacles, occlusions, and distances.
